## Added source-claim units

### EVID-CONT-001 — direct October 2000 missile-restraint pledge

- Source: [Los Angeles Times, 25 October 2000](https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2000-oct-25-mn-41711-story.html)
- Locator: article paragraphs beginning “Kim Jong Il… promised” and “Kim’s pledge…”; lines 248–264 in the retrieved page.
- Claim: During Madeleine Albright’s October 2000 visit, Kim Jong-Il promised that North Korea would not launch another long-range ballistic missile and discussed abandoning missile development and export in exchange for nonmilitary satellite-launch assistance.
- Period fit: Direct; 23–24 October 2000.
- Ruler attribution: Direct; attributed to Kim’s own pledge and conversation with Albright.
- Contrary evidence: The same article records continuing missile exports and unresolved formal agreement; this does not establish completed disarmament.
- Links: 1B.1, 1B.2, 1B.4, 1B.8; 2B.1, 2B.6; 8B.6.
- Disposition: `final_evidence`.

### EVID-CONT-002 — official U.S. account of 2000 nuclear/missile diplomacy

- Source: [U.S. government report, GovInfo, 106th Congress](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CDOC-106hdoc311/pdf/CDOC-106hdoc311.pdf)
- Locator: pp. 5 and 11; paragraphs covering the May 2000 Kumchang-ni visit, October Joint Communiqué, missile talks, and Albright’s 23–24 October meeting.
- Claim: The May 2000 U.S. visit to Kumchang-ni found no evidence contradicting the prior assessment; the October communiqué reaffirmed the missile-test moratorium, both sides rejected hostile intent, and Kim’s proposal linked missile restraint to foreign satellite launches.
- Period fit: Direct; official report issued during 2000.
- Ruler attribution: Direct for Kim’s proposal and meeting; institutional attribution for DPRK commitments is qualified.
- Contrary evidence: The report says the U.S. continued pressing concerns about indigenous missile development and exports, and the moratorium applied while talks continued.
- Links: 1B.1, 1B.3, 1B.4, 1B.8, 1B.10; 2B.1, 2B.6, 2B.10; 8B.6.
- Disposition: `final_evidence`.

### EVID-CONT-003 — conditional nature of the 2000 moratorium

- Source: same [GovInfo report](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CDOC-106hdoc311/pdf/CDOC-106hdoc311.pdf)
- Locator: p. 11, paragraphs stating that the moratorium continued “while talks on the missile issue continue.”
- Claim: The 2000 missile moratorium was conditional rather than an unconditional abandonment of missile capability.
- Period fit: Direct; 2000.
- Ruler attribution: Directly linked to the DPRK position and Kim’s proposal, but not proof of a private order.
- Contrary evidence: EVID-CONT-001 records a stronger public pledge, while the official report preserves the narrower conditional formulation.
- Links: 1B.4, 1B.8, 1B.10; 2B.6; 7B.8; 8B.6.
- Disposition: `final_evidence`.

### EVID-CONT-004 — Kim Jong-Il decree temporarily reducing penalties for food-motivated crossings

- Source: [Human Rights Watch, The Invisible Exodus](https://www.hrw.org/report/2002/11/19/invisible-exodus/north-koreans-peoples-republic-china)
- Locator: paragraphs 257–259; quoted former border guard testimony.
- Claim: According to multiple NGO sources and a former border guard, a Kim Jong-Il decree effective after 16 February 2000 stated that people crossing the border because they needed food should be allowed to live; the reported policy operated until 10 October 2000.
- Period fit: Direct target-period policy evidence, though based on retrospective interviews published in 2002.
- Ruler attribution: Directly attributed by the witness to a decree of Kim Jong-Il; confidence remains medium because the decree is not independently available as a primary document.
- Contrary evidence: The same passage lists aggravating factors leading to reeducation camps or possible execution; the report also documents harsh treatment of repatriated people in April 2000.
- Links: 3B.1, 3B.2, 3B.6, 3B.9; 6B.1, 6B.6; 8B.8, 8B.9.
- Disposition: `final_evidence` with qualified attribution.

### EVID-CONT-005 — April 2000 repatriation abuse

- Source: [Human Rights Watch, The Invisible Exodus](https://www.hrw.org/report/2002/11/19/invisible-exodus/north-koreans-peoples-republic-china)
- Locator: paragraphs 271–276; former border guard’s April 2000 repatriation testimony.
- Claim: A former border guard reported that North Korean National Security Agency officials subjected repatriated people to degrading treatment, confiscation of clothing, interrogation, and threats of secret killing or imprisonment.
- Period fit: Direct; April 2000 incident.
- Ruler attribution: Institutional/security-agency attribution; no direct evidence that Kim personally ordered this specific episode.
- Contrary evidence: EVID-CONT-004 reports a temporary leniency decree for first-time food-motivated crossings, showing policy variation rather than a uniform rule.
- Links: 3B.1, 3B.2, 3B.4, 3B.6, 3B.9; 4B.3, 4B.9.
- Disposition: `final_evidence`, attribution-qualified.

### EVID-CONT-006 — 2000 UN humanitarian program and agricultural recovery plan

- Source: [UN Consolidated Inter-Agency Appeal record](https://digitallibrary.un.org/record/378997); [FAO aid-project chapter](https://www.fao.org/4/y4756e/y4756e0a.htm)
- Locator: UN appeal metadata identifies the January–December 2000 appeal; FAO section “UN consolidated Inter-Agency appeal,” paragraphs describing the double-cropping programme and 2000 agricultural inputs.
- Claim: The 2000 UN appeal sought coordinated food, health, and agricultural assistance; FAO’s programme supplied fertilizer, pesticides, and tools for the 2000 spring and main planting seasons.
- Period fit: Direct; 2000 programme year.
- Ruler attribution: Assistance was requested and implemented through DPRK institutions, but this does not by itself establish Kim’s personal direction.
- Contrary evidence: Reliance on international inputs demonstrates continuing domestic production and welfare vulnerability rather than autonomous policy success.
- Links: 5B.3, 5B.6, 5B.8, 5B.9; 6B.1, 6B.2, 6B.6; 8B.2, 8B.7, 8B.8.
- Disposition: `final_evidence` as institutional/context evidence, not personal attribution.

### EVID-CONT-007 — DPRK’s own 2000 civil-and-political-rights account

- Source: [UN Human Rights Committee record, CCPR/C/PRK/2000/2](https://digitallibrary.un.org/record/428347); [Refworld mirror](https://www.refworld.org/reference/statepartiesrep/hrc/2000/19523)
- Locator: report metadata and sections describing elections to the Supreme People’s Assembly, voting eligibility, and party affiliation.
- Claim: In its 4 May 2000 submission, the DPRK formally represented that citizens’ voting rights were exercised without discrimination based on education, party affiliation, political view, or religion.
- Period fit: Direct; report dated 4 May 2000, describing the operative constitutional/legal framework.
- Ruler attribution: Institutional self-description; not evidence that Kim personally respected or implemented these rights.
- Contrary evidence: The report is a state submission and does not independently verify electoral competition, candidate selection, or freedom from coercion.
- Links: 4B.1, 4B.2, 4B.7; 7B.1, 7B.8.
- Disposition: `context` / contrary-evidence control, not affirmative ruler evidence.

### EVID-CONT-008 — 2000 economic-policy implementation gap

- Source: [Washington Post, 12 September 2002](https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/politics/2002/09/13/a-taste-of-capitalism-in-n-korea/95f6e777-84b3-4864-93a1-cdfbde9c8724/)
- Locator: paragraphs 60–70 and 92–95.
- Claim: The article records that North Korea cancelled planned U.S. business delegations in May and August 2000 and failed to issue visas for a December 2000 delegation, indicating an implementation and credibility gap in external economic engagement.
- Period fit: Direct events in 2000; publication is retrospective.
- Ruler attribution: Regime-level attribution; the article does not establish that Kim personally made each cancellation decision.
- Contrary evidence: The same article reports that Kim later approved the July 2002 economic measures and that some limited private-farming and joint-venture provisions originated in the 1998 constitutional framework.
- Links: 5B.1, 5B.4, 5B.7, 5B.10; 8B.2, 8B.6, 8B.7, 8B.8.
- Disposition: `final_evidence`, institutional attribution only.

## Manifest changes required

Add the eight units above with stable IDs and the listed dispositions.

Change existing entries:

- `EVID-EE`: change from unqualified `final_evidence` to `context` or `final_evidence_qualified`; the cited State Department language is multi-year and does not establish a Kim-issued 2000 shoot-to-kill order.
- `EVID-PPP`: retain `discovery_only`; do not use the Grokipedia health-training claim.
- `EVID-KKKK`: retain `context`; the insurance-scam payment occurred in 2003 and cannot support a 2000 personal-benefit claim.
- `EVID-K` and `EVID-L`: retain as multi-year `context`; they do not independently establish 2000 transfers or Kim’s personal direction.
- Remove researcher conclusions such as “net positive,” “strongly saturated,” and “direct” personal responsibility where the ledger only establishes institutional conduct.

The recoverable gaps now have direct additions for 1B, 2B, 3B, 4B, 5B, 6B, and 8B. No defensible new 2000 source was located for internal nuclear safety appointments, dual-use risk governance, military-failure accountability, or a target-year public correction episode; those remain `research_blocked`, not `no_evidence_found`.
